text:
Maria: Starting staged rollout for v2.14.0 — ramp 5% -> 20% over 10m. Change window is active. @Jake you're SRE lead for this canary.

deploybot: deploybot triggered rollout v2.14.0 canary (5% -> 20%). Initiated at 1849997777. Release ref: rc/v2.14.0. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/release/v2.14.0

Jake: watching metrics now. will shout if p95 > 200ms or error rate spikes.

Linda: Heads-up — release notes posted (kv-cache eviction fix + micro-optimizations). No DB schema changes.

Anna: Seeing early signs in eu-west-1: 502s up and kvcache OOM traces in pods at the ~5% stage. Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/abcd/eu-west1-overview

Jake: Confirming — 502 rate jumped from 1.8% -> 6.2% in last 3m, p95 latency 120ms -> 410ms. @Maria recommend hold.

Maria: HOLD the rollout. @deploybot pin traffic back to v2.13.9 for eu-west-1 and stop further ramping. Do not auto-retry.

deploybot: Received command: pin traffic -> v2.13.9 region=eu-west-1. Executing: /ops/pin --to v2.13.9 --region eu-west-1 --no-auto-retry

ops-bot: Snapshotting cluster & gathering logs: /archives/1849997777-euw-logs.tar.gz. Pods: redwood-llm-1..4; attaching last 200 lines of kube logs.

Jake: Recommend rollback on eu-west-1 to v2.13.9 cluster-wide and apply temporary mitigations (reduce batch size, disable prefetch).

Maria: Agreed. Linda please prep rollback blurb for release notes + support comms. Approving immediate rollback.

Linda: Drafting rollback note now — will post and ping support.

deploybot: Rollback initiated: target=v2.13.9, scope=eu-west-1. Command: /deploy rollback --to v2.13.9 --region eu-west-1 --reason "kvcache OOM -> 502 spike"

deploybot: Rollback progress: draining new pods, shifting traffic, reconciling service routes. ETA ~4m.

deploybot: Rollback complete. Traffic restored to v2.13.9 at 100% in eu-west-1. Canary for v2.14.0 halted.

Anna: Monitoring — 502s trending back down, p95 now ~145ms. Looks stable so far. :thumbsup:

Jake: Filing a follow-up incident and postmortem. I'll include timeline, metrics, and proposed fixes (kvcache guardrails + memory limits + smaller batch defaults).

Maria: Thanks everyone. We'll re-run canary after the kv-cache fix and a full sign-off from SRE/infra. Change window remains open but no further ramp until engineers greenlight. :white_check_mark:
